rules.title: Repeated SSH authentication failures
rules.summary: A source generated a concentrated authentication-failure burst against the controlled decoy gateway.

strategy.name: Authentication pressure correlation
strategy.objective: Identify source-bound authentication pressure while distinguishing a rapid burst from normal retries.

telemetryRequirements.purpose: Differentiate authentication failures from other controlled event types.
Correlate attempts to one lab source within the configured window.
Measure the bounded burst window without relying on arrival order.

investigationQuestions: Does one source meet the configured failure threshold within the correlation window?
Is a privileged username candidate present in the controlled event set?
triageGuidance.dispositionBoundary: Treat a threshold match as suspicious in the lab; use the known-benign scenario to verify that ordinary administrative access does not create a case.

expectedBenignCases: Scheduled service retries and users repeatedly entering an incorrect password.

severityGuidance.rationale: A concentrated burst against a lab decoy warrants analyst review.

riskScoreFactors.label: Failed attempts
riskScoreFactors.rationale: Failure count meets or exceeds the configured threshold.

riskScoreFactors.label: Source concentration
riskScoreFactors.rationale: Events are correlated to one source IP.

riskScoreFactors.label: Privileged targeting
riskScoreFactors.rationale: The event set includes a root account candidate.

rules.title: Successful login after repeated failures
rules.summary: A successful authentication followed a concentrated series of failures from the same source.

strategy.name: Post-authentication context correlation
strategy.objective: Assess a later authentication success using the immediately preceding failure sequence and bounded source context.

telemetryRequirements.purpose: Bind the failures and success to the same controlled source.
Confirm the transition occurs inside the defined correlation window.

investigationQuestions: Did the same lab source produce both the failure sequence and the later success?
Does the success remain inside the configured correlation window after the failures?
triageGuidance.dispositionBoundary: A successful login after mistakes can be benign; evaluate this rule alongside the benign-admin scenario and documented source context.

expectedBenignCases: A legitimate user can make several mistakes before successful authentication.

severityGuidance.rationale: Success after a concentrated failure sequence requires context.

riskScoreFactors.label: Prior failed attempts
riskScoreFactors.rationale: Previous failures were linked to the same source.

riskScoreFactors.label: Authentication success
riskScoreFactors.rationale: A login success followed the failure sequence.

riskScoreFactors.label: Temporal proximity
riskScoreFactors.rationale: The transition occurred within the configured correlation window.

rules.title: Multi-stage decoy engagement and discovery
rules.summary: Correlated credential activity, decoy engagement, and discovery-like behavior formed a complete lab attack story.

strategy.name: Multi-stage behavior sequence correlation
strategy.objective: Require a complete, ordered synthetic sequence before elevating a discovery-like observation.

telemetryRequirements.purpose: Require the controlled credential, decoy, and discovery event categories.
Keep every stage attributable to one lab source.
Identify allowlisted discovery-like command evidence without storing raw TTY logs.
Validate stage order inside the bounded correlation window.

investigationQuestions: Are credential activity, decoy engagement, and discovery evidence all present for one source?
Do the observed discovery events meet the configured minimum without including raw session content?
triageGuidance.dispositionBoundary: Individual inventory commands are not sufficient; the critical lab story requires every configured stage and remains confined to controlled synthetic telemetry.

expectedBenignCases: Individual inventory commands without correlated credential activity should not trigger this rule.

severityGuidance.rationale: A full credential-to-decoy-to-discovery sequence is the highest-risk lab story.

riskScoreFactors.label: Credential activity
riskScoreFactors.rationale: The sequence begins with repeated authentication failures and a later success.

riskScoreFactors.label: Decoy engagement
riskScoreFactors.rationale: The source opened a controlled decoy session.

riskScoreFactors.label: Discovery sequence
riskScoreFactors.rationale: Discovery-like command events followed the session.

rules.title: Low-and-slow authentication pressure
rules.summary: A source sustained authentication failures across a longer bounded window, meeting the controlled low-and-slow pressure contract without matching the rapid-burst profile.

strategy.name: Authentication pressure correlation
strategy.objective: Identify sustained source-bound authentication pressure while keeping ordinary retry behavior outside the rule boundary.

telemetryRequirements.purpose: Restrict correlation to controlled authentication failures.
Keep the sustained sequence attributable to one synthetic source.
Verify both the longer minimum span and the bounded maximum correlation window.

investigationQuestions: Does one source meet the failure threshold across the required minimum span without exceeding the maximum window?
Is the sequence distinct from documented scheduled retries and below-threshold activity?
triageGuidance.dispositionBoundary: Treat the controlled match as a sustained-pressure exercise only; ordinary retries, insufficient counts, and rapid bursts belong to different lab boundaries.

expectedBenignCases: Scheduled service retries and intermittent administrative mistakes that do not meet the stated count and span contract.

severityGuidance.rationale: Sustained controlled pressure deserves review but remains below the complete multi-stage lab story.

riskScoreFactors.label: Sustained failure count
riskScoreFactors.rationale: Failure count meets the configured low-and-slow threshold.

riskScoreFactors.label: Minimum time span
riskScoreFactors.rationale: The activity persists long enough to meet the sustained-pressure contract.

riskScoreFactors.label: Source continuity
riskScoreFactors.rationale: Every correlated failure comes from the same controlled source.

rules.title: Unapproved synthetic access-policy change after login
rules.summary: A successful synthetic login was followed by a source-bound access-policy change that lacked the required controlled approval marker.

strategy.name: Authorized-change context correlation
strategy.objective: Separate an unapproved synthetic access-policy change from a documented authorized-change control.

telemetryRequirements.purpose: Require a controlled authentication success and synthetic policy-change event.
Bind the login and change event to one controlled source.
Verify the policy change follows the login inside the bounded window.
Distinguish the synthetic unapproved-change exercise from the authorized-change negative control.

investigationQuestions: Did a controlled authentication success precede the synthetic policy change for the same source?
Is the approval-state marker explicitly false rather than missing or approved?
triageGuidance.dispositionBoundary: This rule models a synthetic training event only; it does not inspect or alter real access policies and cannot establish production authorization context.

expectedBenignCases: A documented synthetic authorized policy change and a policy-change event without the required preceding login context.

severityGuidance.rationale: A source-bound unapproved synthetic change after login is a focused analyst-context exercise.

riskScoreFactors.label: Source-bound login
riskScoreFactors.rationale: A controlled authentication success precedes the change from the same source.

riskScoreFactors.label: Unapproved change marker
riskScoreFactors.rationale: The synthetic approval-state marker is explicitly false.

riskScoreFactors.label: Temporal proximity
riskScoreFactors.rationale: The change occurs inside the configured correlation window.

scenarios.label: Full pipeline story
scenarios.description: Brute-force attempts progress to decoy interaction and discovery behavior.

useCase.learningObjective: Validate that a correlated credential-to-decoy-to-discovery story continues to produce every intended detection after a rule or parser change.
validationSteps: Replay the controlled scenario from the analyst workspace.
Confirm that all three expected rules produce cases with one source-bound timeline.
Compare the observed rule IDs with the evaluation matrix before accepting the change.
useCase.expectedOutcome: Three detections are present: repeated failures, success after failure, and the multi-stage sequence.

scenarios.label: Credential probe
scenarios.description: Authentication failures followed by a successful login.

useCase.learningObjective: Practice deciding whether a later authentication success should be escalated by reviewing source continuity and the configured time window.
validationSteps: Replay the controlled credential-probe scenario.
Inspect the failure and success evidence for one source and the defined correlation window.
Record a disposition that cites the triage boundary rather than the technique label alone.
useCase.expectedOutcome: Two detections are present and the case remains explainable as a lab signal that requires contextual review.

scenarios.label: Benign admin activity
scenarios.description: Normal administrative access that should not create a case.

useCase.learningObjective: Demonstrate that ordinary authorized administration and isolated inventory activity remain outside the current detection boundaries.
validationSteps: Replay the known-benign administrative scenario.
Confirm that the evaluation matrix reports zero observed detections and zero false positives.
Use the result as a negative control when revising a related correlation rule.
useCase.expectedOutcome: No case is created; the scenario remains a documented negative control.

scenarios.label: Threshold boundary
scenarios.description: Exactly one fewer authentication failure than the repeated-failure threshold.

useCase.learningObjective: Prove that the repeated-failure rule begins only at its declared threshold rather than alerting on nearby but insufficient activity.
validationSteps: Replay the edge-case scenario with one fewer failure than the configured threshold.
Confirm that no repeated-failure detection is observed.
Change the threshold only with a corresponding scenario and regression-test update.
useCase.expectedOutcome: No case is created, demonstrating a precise and testable correlation boundary.

scenarios.label: Low-and-slow authentication pressure
scenarios.description: Sustained authentication failures from one controlled source across a longer bounded window.

useCase.learningObjective: Practice distinguishing sustained authentication pressure from both rapid bursts and ordinary scheduled retries.
validationSteps: Replay the sustained-pressure scenario from the analyst workspace.
Confirm that the rapid-burst rule does not fire because the sequence exceeds its shorter window.
Validate the low-and-slow case against its count, source, minimum span, and maximum-window contract.
useCase.expectedOutcome: One medium-severity low-and-slow authentication-pressure detection is created.

scenarios.label: Scheduled service retries
scenarios.description: Intermittent controlled service retries that remain below the sustained-pressure count contract.

useCase.learningObjective: Use a documented retry pattern as a negative control for the low-and-slow authentication rule.
validationSteps: Replay the scheduled-retry scenario.
Confirm that the observed failure count remains below the low-and-slow threshold.
Record the no-alert result as evidence that ordinary retries stay outside the current boundary.
useCase.expectedOutcome: No case is created; the scenario remains a negative control.

scenarios.label: Low-and-slow threshold boundary
scenarios.description: One fewer sustained failure than the low-and-slow authentication-pressure threshold.

useCase.learningObjective: Prove that sustained-pressure detection begins only when both the configured count and span are met.
validationSteps: Replay the low-and-slow boundary scenario.
Verify that the span is sufficient but the failure count is one event below the threshold.
Confirm that no case is created before changing the detection threshold.
useCase.expectedOutcome: No case is created, demonstrating a precise sustained-pressure count boundary.

scenarios.label: Unapproved synthetic policy change
scenarios.description: A controlled login is followed by a synthetic access-policy change with an explicit unapproved marker.

useCase.learningObjective: Practice using authentication context and an approval-state signal together before elevating a synthetic change event.
validationSteps: Replay the unapproved synthetic policy-change scenario.
Confirm the login and change share a source and occur in the configured window.
Inspect the explicit unapproved marker and compare the result to the authorized-change control.
useCase.expectedOutcome: One high-severity synthetic access-policy-change detection is created.

scenarios.label: Authorized synthetic policy change
scenarios.description: A controlled login is followed by a synthetic access-policy change with an explicit approved marker.

useCase.learningObjective: Validate that an authorized synthetic change remains outside the unapproved-change detection boundary.
validationSteps: Replay the authorized synthetic policy-change scenario.
Confirm the policy-change event carries an explicit approved marker.
Verify that no unapproved-change case is created despite matching source and timing context.
useCase.expectedOutcome: No case is created; approval state remains a required observable control.

scenarios.label: Synthetic policy change without login context
scenarios.description: An unapproved-marked synthetic policy-change event without the required preceding authentication context.

useCase.learningObjective: Demonstrate that a policy-change signal alone does not satisfy the current correlation contract.
validationSteps: Replay the policy-change-without-auth edge scenario.
Confirm the change marker is unapproved but no matching authentication success is present.
Verify that the detector does not create a case when the required context is absent.
useCase.expectedOutcome: No case is created, preserving the login-context requirement.
